title: How to set up events in Plausible and Fathom
description: How custom events / goals work in Plausible and Fathom — when they are enough, how to keep naming simple, and when to graduate to GA4 or PostHog.
quickAnswer: **Plausible** and **Fathom** are pageview-first. Add a handful of **custom events or goals** for key CTAs (signup, contact, download). They will not replace product funnels — and that is intentional for privacy-first marketing sites.

sections.title: Goals, not giant taxonomies
sections.content:
These tools shine when you track **a few conversions** on top of traffic reports. Aim for five or fewer named goals on a marketing site.

If you need nested funnels, account-level retention, or experiment assignment, look at PostHog or GA4 instead.

sections.title: Plausible custom events
sections.content:
Plausible supports custom events via a small JS API or attribute-based triggers (depending on your setup). Name events clearly (`Signup`, `Demo Request`) and verify them in the realtime dashboard.

Billing is primarily **pageviews**, so events are about clarity — not a separate meter in the same way event-based products charge.

sections.title: Fathom events / goals
sections.content:
Fathom’s model likewise centers on simple site analytics plus goals for conversions. Keep the same discipline: stable names, one purpose per goal, test after deploy.

Compare pricing and UX with [Plausible vs Fathom](/compare/plausible-vs-fathom/).

sections.title: When to graduate
sections.content:
Graduate when weekly questions outgrow "traffic + one CTA": multi-step onboarding, feature adoption, or ads-heavy attribution. Until then, a light script and a short goal list beat an unused event warehouse.

Script weight context: both sit in our light [performance matrix](/learn/analytics-script-performance/).
